text:
alex_support: Hey team, customer Jane reported a mid-stream disconnect during a streaming completion. They got a partial response (~420 tokens) then the client closed. Billing shows tokens counted for the partial output, and the client got no retry/resume behavior.

jane_customer: Hi — happened on iPhone on my mobile hotspot. App showed 'stream ended' and text truncated. I have a recording and logs. Noticed it happened when switching from home WiFi -> VPN.

liz_cs: Thanks @jane_customer. Filing escalation. Can you attach the session id and the exact time? We need client logs and the request id.

ajax_support: session id is in the attached screenshot: session=abc123-stream-2026-03-16-18:07. Customer said approx 18:07:12 UTC.

maya_eng_oncall: Looking. Do we have server-side request_id/trace for abc123? Also what error code did the client see (502/ERR_CONNECTION_RESET/etc)?

jane_customer: Client shows ECONNRESET then reconnect attempt. App log: \"stream: close: code=0, reason=EOF, socket=ECONNRESET\".

tom_mobile_dev: Quick thought — mobile transitions + VPN often change NAT mapping and result in TCP RST. Does the SDK send any resume token or response_id to continue?

ajax_support: Customer is on our JS SDK v1.8.3 (webview). I asked them to paste the initial headers. They included: 

Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Request-ID: abc123

maya_eng_oncall: Got logs from server for X-Request-ID abc123. Server stream started and produced 420 tokens then connection closed from client side (TCP FIN). No server error emitted. On our side we flagged stream as completed because client closed the connection.

maya_eng_oncall: Repro hypothesis: client-side network change => TCP reset => client didn't attempt to re-open a new stream with resume semantics (we don't offer automatic resume by default). So app lost the remainder of the generation.

alex_support: Customer complains they were billed for the partial output. Is there billing guidance?

billing_bot: Per billing policy, tokens streamed before connection termination are billable. Support can issue ad-hoc credit for unreliable network cases. Use billing-credits template.

liz_cs: I'll offer a one-time credit while engineering investigates.

maya_eng_oncall: Mitigations / next steps:
- Short term: advise customer to enable keepalive pings at the transport layer and increase client-side socket timeout to tolerate transient NAT changes. For mobile (iOS) webview: set fetch timeout to 60s and enable reconnect/backoff.
- Mid term: SDK change — expose a resume token argument that the server can use to rehydrate KV cache and continue from last token for idempotent streams. This requires model checkpointing for streaming sessions.
- Server policy: consider marking streams that close due to client-side resets as \"incomplete\" and surface a refund flow for credits (manual for now).

alex_support: Can you paste a minimal repro to share with customer?

maya_eng_oncall: Minimal repro steps for internal triage:
1) Start a streaming request with long generation (e.g., max_tokens=1500) using text/event-stream.
2) While stream is active, flip network on device or enable VPN so NAT mapping changes (I use macOS hotspot -> cellular on my phone).
3) Observe client ECONNRESET and truncated event sequence. Server will show completed stream with no error.

Example curl to start stream (for repro):

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESPONSE_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-stream","input":"long prompt...","max_tokens":1500}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate

Note: -N to disable buffering.

alex_support: Thanks. @tom_mobile_dev any SDK guidance we can give Jane now?

tom_mobile_dev: For iOS webview / mobile native:
- Use incremental rendering with a small processing buffer.
- Add network-change listener and if connection changes, re-open stream and attempt resume if you persisted last-event-id.
- If resume not available, on reconnect call the API with the same prompt and a low temperature / deterministic seeds so output is closer to original.

jane_customer: Would love a client-side snippet to persist last-event-id.

tom_mobile_dev: Example (pseudo):

let lastEventId = null;
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers });
es.onmessage = (e) => { lastEventId = e.lastEventId || lastEventId; render(e.data); }
es.onerror = () => { // detect network change, try reconnect with lastEventId param }

maya_eng_oncall: Follow-ups for engineering:
- Track feature request: resume-on-reconnect for streaming sessions (design doc).
- Add server-side telemetry to tag client-close vs server-error and export metric: stream_incomplete_client_reset_count.

alex_support: Liz will handle credit. Maya, can you estimate ETA for a design doc?

maya_eng_oncall: I'll draft a short design doc by EOD tomorrow describing resume token format and expected compatibility with quantized KV cache. No promises on release date.

liz_cs: Sent credit to Jane. Closing loop on customer side & asking for confirmation. :white_check_mark:

jane_customer: Thanks all — workaround applied and credit received. Will test again and report. Appreciate the speedy help. :pray:

alex_support: Marking this thread as escalated->resolved. Adding tag: mobile-network-handoff.

notes: session abc123 artifacts: server-trace=trace-98765, sdk-version=1.8.3, platform=iOS-webview, repro-curl-included, billing-credit=one-time-5USD
